newsitem.title: USA: Detroit airport eyes $640 mln of revenue bonds.
newsitem.headline: Detroit airport eyes $640 mln of revenue bonds.

text.p: A financing plan for a $1 billion expansion of Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport includes $640 million of general airport revenue bonds, a county official said Friday.

Susan Kopinksi, the county's deputy chief financial officer, said the plan worked out between the county and Northwest Airlines, indicates the county would sell the bonds to help finance a new midfield terminal and other airport improvements.
Northwest would be a major user of the terminal along with other international carriers, according to Allan Johnson, Northwest's regional director for airport affairs.

Kopinski said there was no timetable yet for selling the bonds and that no underwriting firms have been selected. She added the county would probably send out a request for proposals for underwriters.
She added the bonds would be backed by airport revenues and that she does not expect at this time to sell bonds backed solely by revenues from the airport's $3 passenger facility charge.

In fact, the financing plan indicates that a total of $239 million of passenger fee revenues would be used on a pay-as-you-go basis for the project. The airport currently collects about $36 million from the per passenger fee a year.
The plan also includes federal and state of Michigan grant funds.
Johnson said the $65 million in grants from Michigan would be used to pay for a cargo building and maintenance facility for Northwest.

County and Northwest Airline officials unveiled the expansion plan last May. In addition to the terminal, the plan includes a fourth parallel runway, a noise mitigation program and improvements to existing terminals.
